name: Sculpfun E1 Pro 21W
tagline: Enclosed 21W CoreXY diode with camera and air pump included, IR module optional
tldr: The Sculpfun E1 Pro puts a 21W diode on a CoreXY gantry inside a Class 1 enclosure with a 400 × 320 mm work area, built-in camera, air pump and honeycomb bed. Sculpfun claims 600 mm/s engraving and 12 mm wood in one pass. A Dual bundle adds a swappable 3W 1064 nm IR module for metal. Launched June 2026; no in-depth independent review yet.
mainObjective: Enclosed diode engraving and wood cutting on a mid-size bed at an open-frame price

priceRange.note: $849 single 21W, $1,149 Dual with 3W IR module (Sculpfun store, Oct 2026)

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cut: Basswood & plywood up to 12 mm (claimed, one pass)
cannot: Objects taller than 42 mm (30 mm with honeycomb)

pros: Sculpfun claims 12 mm wood in a single pass
Cuts 3 mm basswood squares in ~3–5 min at 8–15 mm/s in our benchmarks
Compact ~0.06 × 0.08 mm spot despite the higher power
cons: $849 for the single-laser version, $350 more than the base E1
More smoke per job: the exhaust hose must be routed outside, not just out of the enclosure
Hardwood and dense plywood cut much slower than basswood figures suggest
beginnerNotes: This profile is the E1 Pro (21W) in the Sculpfun E1 line. Compare it with the 12W E1: choose the E1 Pro if you plan to cut wood regularly. The Dual bundle is worth it only if you want to mark bare metal: the IR module can also be bought later.
proTips: Keep the air pump on for every cut and check focus with the gauge before each job, since there is no auto-focus. For tall objects, remove the honeycomb or add the metal risers Sculpfun sells for the E1 series. Vent the exhaust outside or add the SP1 purifier.

faq.question: How much faster does the E1 Pro cut than the base E1?
faq.answer: Sculpfun claims 12 mm of wood in one pass for the Pro against 8 mm for the 12W E1. In our benchmarks the Pro cuts a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood in about 3–5 min at 8–15 mm/s, against 5–8 min for the 12W. For $350 more ($849 against $499) you roughly halve cut times.

faq.question: What does the Dual version add, and can I add infrared later?
faq.answer: The Dual adds a 3W infrared module for marking metal and some plastics: $1,149 against $849 for the single 21W (Sculpfun store, October 2026). The IR3 module alone costs $499, so the Dual saves about $200 if you are sure you want metal marking. Adding it later remains possible.

faq.question: Can the E1 Pro cut clear acrylic or metal?
faq.answer: No. The 455 nm blue diode passes through clear acrylic, and neither the diode nor the 3W infrared module cuts metal. The infrared module marks stainless steel and other metals; for cutting clear acrylic you need a CO₂ laser.

editorialDepth.advantages: The E1 Pro brings 21W cutting power into a closed Class 1 box for well under $1,000, with camera and air pump included. The CoreXY gantry is built for speed, and the 400 × 320 mm area covers most signs, boxes and batches of coasters.
editorialDepth.limitations: Clearance is shallow (30 mm with the honeycomb), focus is manual, and the 12 mm cutting figure is a manufacturer claim. Clear acrylic remains out of reach, as with any diode.

standoutFeatures.title: Thick cuts in one pass
standoutFeatures.body: Sculpfun rates the 21W module for 12 mm wood in a single pass, a level usually reserved for open-frame 20W+ machines.

standoutFeatures.title: Fine spot at high power
standoutFeatures.body: About 0.06 × 0.08 mm in our profile, so engraving detail holds up despite the cutting power.

standoutFeatures.title: Dual laser option
standoutFeatures.body: The $1,149 Dual kit adds a 3W infrared module for marking metals, $200 less than buying the module separately.
